unit.label: Confirmation, comparison & birthday wishes
unit.title: Happy Birthday and Best Wishes
unit.description: Finish the birthday topic with confirmation questions, equality comparisons, birthday wishes, and a four-objective capstone.

goal.text: 祝你生日快樂、萬事如意、心想事成。
goal.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēngrì kuàilè, wànshì rúyì, xīnxiǎng shìchéng.
goal.meaning: Happy birthday; may everything go your way and all your wishes come true.

lessons.title: The Same Birthday Food
lessons.subtitle: Learn 蛋糕 and close the food part of the conversation.

steps.prompt: 蛋糕 means…
steps.explanation: 蛋糕 is cake.

steps.prompt: Which earlier verb appears in 今天我也訂了一個生日蛋糕?
steps.explanation: The sentence reuses 訂, 'order / reserve in advance'.

steps.prompt: In 跟你們一樣，吃蛋糕。, what is the speaker saying?
options: We eat cake too, just like you.
steps.answer: We eat cake too, just like you.
steps.explanation: 一樣 signals that the birthday practice is the same here.

lessons.title: You're Confirming, Right?
lessons.subtitle: Use 是不是 when you expect confirmation.

steps.prompt: What is the main job of 是不是 here?
options: ask only for a new location
steps.explanation: The pattern distinguishes confirmation from neutral information-seeking.

steps.prompt: Which is grammatical with 比?
options: 你比不比他高？ as the required form
steps.explanation: Ordinary A-not-A is unavailable in this environment.

steps.prompt: Which context best motivates 是不是?
options: You already suspect your friend is busy and want confirmation.
You have no idea what their name is.
steps.answer: You already suspect your friend is busy and want confirmation.
steps.explanation: Context makes the confirmation reading clear.

steps.prompt: A 跟 B 一樣 means…
options: A and B are the same/alike
A is definitely taller than B
steps.answer: A and B are the same/alike
steps.explanation: 跟…一樣 is an equality comparison.

steps.prompt: Where can a shared property go?
steps.explanation: 一樣高 = equally tall.

lessons.title: Same or Different?
lessons.subtitle: Control negation scope and question forms.

steps.prompt: A 跟 B 不一樣 says…
options: A and B differ in the relevant quality.
B is simply not the comparison target.
steps.answer: A and B differ in the relevant quality.
steps.explanation: 不 before 一樣 negates sameness.

steps.prompt: A 不跟 B 一樣… primarily changes…
steps.explanation: 不 before 跟 has different scope.

steps.prompt: Which question forms can both be used?
options: 一樣不一樣？ and 是不是一樣？
steps.answer: 一樣不一樣？ and 是不是一樣？
steps.explanation: Both question forms are valid.

steps.prompt: Which says 'My birthday is different from yours'?
options: 我的生日跟你的生日不一樣。
我的生日不跟你的生日一樣高。
我的生日是不是你的生日。
steps.answer: 我的生日跟你的生日不一樣。
steps.explanation: 不 before 一樣 negates equality.

lessons.title: Kind to Me, Best Wishes
lessons.subtitle: Use 對 + person, 祝, and the fixed birthday wishes.

steps.prompt: In 你對我真好, 對 means…
steps.explanation: This is the productive prepositional use.

steps.prompt: 祝 + person + wish is used to…
steps.explanation: 祝 is a lexical-syntactic frame, not a numbered grammar section.

steps.prompt: How should 萬事如意 and 心想事成 be learned?
options: as two new productive grammar templates
steps.explanation: These examples present conventional auspicious expressions.

steps.prompt: What cultural point is illustrated by these wishes?
options: Congratulatory sayings often use fixed four-character auspicious expressions.
Only one wish may be used.
steps.answer: Congratulatory sayings often use fixed four-character auspicious expressions.
steps.explanation: These two are presented as broadly useful wishes.

lessons.title: Birthday Across Cultures
lessons.subtitle: Use the full birthday toolkit in new birthday scenarios.

steps.prompt: Phone appointment: after class you immediately go meet your friend. Which fits?
steps.explanation: This retrieves the earlier immediate-sequence pattern and the phone-appointment outcome.

steps.prompt: Dietary preferences: which question is useful before choosing dinner?
steps.explanation: This meets the dietary-preference objective.

steps.prompt: A friend eats anything. Which answer fits?
steps.explanation: This retrieves the earlier question-word totality pattern.

steps.prompt: You and your friend both eat cake for birthdays. Which comparison fits?
options: 我們跟你們一樣吃蛋糕。
steps.answer: 我們跟你們一樣吃蛋糕。
steps.explanation: 跟…一樣 + action compares the shared birthday practice.

steps.prompt: Which line gives birthday wishes?
options: 祝你生日快樂、萬事如意。
steps.answer: 祝你生日快樂、萬事如意。
steps.explanation: This meets the wishes objective.

steps.prompt: How should the friend respond?
steps.explanation: The response is 謝謝.

steps.prompt: Which compares two customs as different?
options: 這個傳統跟那個不一樣。
steps.answer: 這個傳統跟那個不一樣。
steps.explanation: This is the comparison objective.

steps.prompt: Which action completes the phone-appointment task?
options: agree on when and where to meet
only say happy birthday with no plan
steps.answer: agree on when and where to meet
steps.explanation: The activity requires arranging the meeting.

lessons.title: Unit 41 Review
lessons.subtitle: Review confirmation, comparison, wishes, and cumulative transfer.

steps.explanation: That is the equality-comparison core.

options: A 跟 B 不一樣
A 不跟 B 一樣 only
steps.answer: A 跟 B 不一樣

糕.note: 糕 gāo appears in 蛋糕 dàngāo, “cake.” It is also used in names of other cakes and prepared foods.
糕.memory: Rice 米 sits beside 羔. The rice component helps you remember that 糕 is a food character.

parts.description: Rice component in 糕: strokes 1–6. Rice 米 sits beside 羔. The rice component helps you remember that 糕 is a food character.

parts.description: Right component in 糕: strokes 7–16. Rice 米 sits beside 羔. The rice component helps you remember that 糕 is a food character.

祝.note: 祝 zhù means “wish” when offering good wishes: 祝你生日快樂, “Wish you a happy birthday.”
祝.memory: A four-stroke 礻 sits beside 兄. Keep 礻 distinct from the five-stroke clothing component 衤.

parts.description: Ritual component in 祝: strokes 1–4. A four-stroke 礻 sits beside 兄. Keep 礻 distinct from the five-stroke clothing component 衤.

parts.label: 兄
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 祝: strokes 5–9. A four-stroke 礻 sits beside 兄. Keep 礻 distinct from the five-stroke clothing component 衤.

u41-shibushi.title: Confirmation questions with 是不是
u41-shibushi.explanation: 是不是 asks the listener to confirm information the speaker already knows, expects, or sees as likely. It is not simply interchangeable with every neutral 嗎 or A-not-A question. This lesson uses 是不是 in environments where ordinary A-not-A is unavailable, including 比 comparisons and 太…了. When multiple grammatical strategies are possible, context must make the confirmation reading clear.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì bú shì zuìjìn tài máng le?
examples.meaning: You've been too busy lately, right?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì bú shì bǐ tā gāo?

examples.text: 臺灣人過生日是不是都吃這些東西？
examples.pinyin: Táiwān rén guò shēngrì shì bú shì dōu chī zhèxiē dōngxi?
examples.meaning: Do Taiwanese people all eat these things for birthdays?

u41-shibushi.remember: Use 是不是 when checking/confirming information, not merely asking neutral new information.

u41-gen-yiyang.title: Comparison with 跟…一樣
u41-gen-yiyang.pattern: A + 跟 + B + 一樣 (+ property)
u41-gen-yiyang.explanation: A 跟 B 一樣 says A and B are the same; a property can follow 一樣 to show equal degree. Put 不 before 一樣 to say the two differ in the relevant quality. Put 不 before 跟 to reject B as the comparison target, often followed by another target. Questions can use 一樣不一樣 or 是不是一樣; both are valid.

examples.text: 我的生日跟你的生日一樣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shēngrì gēn nǐ de shēngrì yíyàng.
examples.meaning: My birthday is the same as yours.
I am as tall as you.

examples.text: 我的生日跟你的生日不一樣。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shēngrì gēn nǐ de shēngrì bù yíyàng.
examples.meaning: My birthday is different from yours.

examples.text: 他不跟我一樣高，跟你一樣高。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù gēn wǒ yíyàng gāo, gēn nǐ yíyàng gāo.
examples.meaning: He isn't as tall as me; he's as tall as you.

u41-gen-yiyang.remember: Same: A 跟 B 一樣. Different quality: A 跟 B 不一樣. Different comparison target: A 不跟 B 一樣. Ask with 一樣不一樣 or 是不是一樣.

u41-cake-source.text: 跟你們一樣，吃蛋糕。今天我也訂了一個生日蛋糕。

u41-cake-source.meaning: The same as you: we eat cake. Today I also ordered a birthday cake.
u41-cake-source.note: Source the conversation turn 10. The first clause is comprehension-first until comparison is formally taught.
